title: Synthesis: equilibrium from both sides
summary: Cumulative synthesis of thermodynamic and kinetic equilibrium, coupled speciation and a carbon-conversion model integrating stoichiometry, bonding, pH, electrochemistry, coordination and evidence.

objectives.description: Reconcile thermodynamic equilibrium and elementary kinetics with standard-state conventions.
Combine equilibria to calculate free and total species while preserving balances.
Design quantitative bidirectional tests of equilibrium and relaxation.
Integrate stoichiometry, bonding, acid speciation, electrochemistry, coordination and kinetics in a defensible model-based report.

preparation.description: Elementary kinetic equilibrium and unit conventions
Temperature and equilibrium; qualify rate statements by the model
Connecting chemical domains in a case study

activities.title: Lecture notes and primary reading
activities.instructions: Work through the notes with the assigned source open. Reproduce each worked calculation or derivation on paper, including its assumptions, before reading the next step. Write one question that remains unresolved.

activities.title: Problem sheet: calculation, explanation and transfer
activities.instructions: Attempt the problems independently first. Use one hint at a time if useful, and record which help you used. Show the reasoning that connects the model and its assumptions to each answer; compare the reference only after a substantial attempt.

activities.title: Return without the notes
activities.instructions: On a later study day, close the notes and reconstruct the core relation and its assumptions, then explain the failure case from the last problem. Compare with your saved work and correct one gap. This practice does not itself certify mastery.

exitCheck.description: Submit the multi-part carbon-conversion capstone: conservation and bonding, pH-dependent electrochemistry and reversible work, acid speciation, charge/product/energy calculations, coordination evidence and a controlled test of equilibrium versus kinetics. Address all six weighted criteria and state model limits. Revisit earlier problem-sheet gaps separately; completion is evidence for integration, not blanket mastery.

commonMisconceptions.claim: At equilibrium the total Gibbs energy must be zero.
commonMisconceptions.correction: The reaction free-energy change vanishes at equilibrium; the system Gibbs energy itself need not be zero.

commonMisconceptions.claim: K always equals an unqualified ratio of rate constants.
commonMisconceptions.correction: The relation depends on the elementary rate law and standard-state factors; differing molecularities require dimensional care.

commonMisconceptions.claim: An imposed-voltage cell is automatically a closed equilibrium system.
commonMisconceptions.correction: External electrical and material reservoirs change the system boundary and may maintain a nonequilibrium state.
